name: Metastability and Temporary Law-Like Regime Law
purpose: Define temporary law-like regimes as metastable organizations of reinforced continuation channels.

candidate_law_statement.informal: A law-like regime is metastable when reinforced continuation channels remain coherent for a bounded span before weakening, transitioning, fracturing, or being replaced.

formal.metastable_regime_candidate: M_U := { C_i ∈ U : C_i remains reinforced, admissible, and mutually coherent within tolerance over bounded continuation depth }
formal.validity_window_candidate: V(M_U) := bounded interval/order-depth over which M_U satisfies persistence, budget, and topology-coherence conditions
formal.lifespan_condition: Life(M_U) depends on reinforcement renewal, decay rate, perturbation load, basin competition, and admissibility budget exhaustion.
formal.transition_condition: Transition(M_U → M_V) occurs when decay, perturbation, or topology transition causes one coherent law-like regime to lose validity while another stabilizes.
formal.temporary_law_clause: Law-like regimes are locally valid, metastable continuation structures, not eternal governing rules.
